Keyword evidence · V6 §14.4 · internal — do not publish

Keyword ownership and evidence

Which Batch 1 page owns which search, what the evidence is, and where a cluster is deliberately owned by a page outside this batch. Source: SE Ranking positions export, Google Australia, 8 September 2026.

161Tracked keywords with a mapped URL
37,840Combined monthly search volume
128SERPs showing an AI Overview — 80% of the set
15Currently ranking in the top 20
97Not in the top 100 today

What the export says

The single most important number here

128 of 161 tracked SERPs carry an AI Overview. That is not a side-issue for this rebuild — it is the reason every page in this batch leads with a 40–55 word self-contained answer directly under the H1, uses real questions as headings, and states specifics rather than adjectives. Pages written that way are the ones that get lifted into the answer block; pages written as marketing copy are not.

The second thing the export shows is where the opportunity actually sits. 97 of the tracked terms do not rank in the top 100 at all, including the largest commercial terms the homepage is mapped to. The site is not being outranked on these — it is not competing for them. That is a different problem, and a more fixable one.

Conflicts raised for approval

Conflict 1 — "website design australia" has two claimants

The export maps website design australia (590/mo, $4.72, AI Overview) to the homepage. The Implementation Pack's New Pages Required sheet assigns "website design australia" (480/KD37) as the primary keyword for the new /locations/ hub. Both cannot own it.

Recommendation: the homepage keeps it. It is already the mapped URL, it is the national agency term, and the pack's own rule R3 says location pages own service-plus-city while the national term stays with the service or brand page. /locations/ should take "web design australia" and the "near me" cluster instead. This needs a decision before /locations/ is written in Batch 2.

Conflict 2 — a position-2 ranking is scheduled to move, and its destination is not in this batch

web design reseller sits at position 2 on /website-design-reseller-service/, with web design reseller program at position 8. That page is also AI Overview cited. It is the strongest white-label asset on the domain by a wide margin.

It is scheduled to 301 into /white-label/reseller-program/, which is P1 in the queue but not in Batch 1. So /white-label/ ships this batch linking to a destination that does not exist yet, and the highest-value redirect in the project has no built destination to QA.

Recommendation: pull /white-label/reseller-program/ forward into Batch 1. It is a P1 page, it is the destination of the riskiest redirect in the migration, and building it alongside /white-label/ means the whole white-label silo can be QA'd as one unit before any redirect fires.

Boundary held — no action needed

/web-design-and-seo/ targets seo website design (390/mo, $14.89 — the highest CPC in the tracked set). /seo-ready-website/ keeps seo ready website, where it holds position 20 and an AI Overview citation. Two terms, two intents, two pages, no overlap. The pack's stated primary for this page — "web design and seo" — is not in the tracked export, so the measured term is used as primary and the pack's term is carried as a secondary.
